The smaller outer bank (counterscarp) is inferred to be the re-cut spoil. Later erosion is not dated: the lowered bank from year 1 CE is a convention; by Stukeley's time bank and ditch were still visible.

The Danes took its eastern half in 877; the western half was ruled by Ealdorman Aethelred and Aethelflaed under West Saxon lordship until Edward the Elder annexed it in 918. The polygon is Mercia proper about 790 under Offa, including Lindsey, the Hwicce, Middlesex and London but not the client kingdoms of Kent, Sussex, Essex and East Anglia. Frontiers were zones of shifting lordship, not lines. Dates are supported here only by Wikipedia, which is a lead rather than verification.

fact_snapshot.value_text: kingdom: Kingdom of the West Saxons
fact_snapshot.detail: 519 is the legendary date of Cerdic; the historical kingdom grew from the Gewisse of the upper Thames in the 7th century. From 825 it also held Kent, Sussex, Surrey and Essex, and from about 886 Alfred styled himself king of the Anglo-Saxons. The polygon is the core kingdom of about 800, before those gains, with Devon included and Cornwall still British. Frontiers were zones of shifting lordship, not lines. Dates are supported here only by Wikipedia, which is a lead rather than verification.

em-app-brunanburh-point.note: The Chronicle poem supports the battle, not Bromborough coordinates. The app already describes more than forty candidate sites and marks the location unknown/low.

em-app-gruffudd.note: The revised DWB article argues 1064; the current app note already preserves that alternative alongside conventional 1063. This does not justify replacing 1063 outright.

em-app-hywel-manuscripts.note: DWB explicitly dates the oldest manuscript to the last quarter of the twelfth century.

em-app-jarrow-start.note: The Cambridge handbook dates the two sites separately. The problem is the Jarrow marker’s 674 onset, not denial that Wearmouth was founded in 674.

em-app-northumbria-start.note: Bede and EH attest earlier Northumbrian unions. A continuous 654 start loses Edwin and Oswald.

em-app-rhodri-powys.note: Thornton’s accessible ODNB extract uses possible control in 855 or later. The overstatement recurs in two polity notes.

em-app-torksey-camp.note: HER gives the northern camp and estimated centre. Moving the shared town/camp point would misplace later phases; identify it as a town reference and add a separate camp feature.

em-app-whitby-end.note: EH explicitly denies knowledge of the precise ninth-century abandonment.

em-app-winchester-largest.note: The edition gives Winchester and Wallingford equal 2,400-hide assessments, not exclusive population rank.

lm-app-lewes-location.note: The Trust’s prose qualifies its own secure-location data box.

lm-app-mynydd-site.note: Coflein’s northern narrative conflicts with its Templeton catalogue point. No replacement exact coordinate is established.

pr-cmp-grimspound-abandon.note: EH states duration unknown and soil/settlement change, not a climate-caused 800 BCE abandonment.

pr-cmp-segontium-end.note: Cadw derives c.394 from coins. That is not an exact evacuation observation.

pr-cmp-stonehenge-roman.note: EH gives no conquest-year destruction. The national and detailed-site ruin boundaries are different modelling conventions.

pr-cmp-uffington-date.note: The exact EH bracket 1740–210 BCE is already in the current uncertainty text, which explicitly calls the chosen 1000 BCE start unmeasured. No replacement year is justified.

em-app-dyrham-class.note: A later document can be attested-documentary without being contemporary testimony. The app already marks low confidence and explains the three-century delay. The Chronicle is a better citation, but the event itself is not newly verified.

em-app-ellendun-transfer.note: The Chronicle distinguishes the victory from Æthelwulf’s subsequent operation, but the app’s summary need not mean instantaneous transfer. The consulted old translation’s annal is 823, not conventional 825; do not change the date on that edition alone.

em-app-english-unification.note: The Chronicle supports contested northern control through 954. The app’s separate Jorvik note already says York was lost again after 927; no claim that every English king continuously held it was found.

lm-app-battle-abbey-approx.note: EH says about 1071; the app summary also says about 1071. Annual display precision remains a general limitation, not a demonstrated erroneous year.

lm-app-beaumaris-incomplete.note: Cadw confirms unfinished gatehouse/towers. The current app already says work petered out and uses an unfinished-castle phase label. No finished detailed Beaumaris model exists in the reviewed dataset.

lm-app-bryn-site.note: Coflein lists alternative hills and negative survey. The app already describes uncertainty and neighbouring hills. Listing Graig Hill and Blacke Hyll explicitly is useful enrichment, not proof the present caveat is false.

lm-app-margam-approx.note: Coflein says around 1147, and the app summary already says about 1147. Do not replace a qualified scalar anchor with another arbitrary year.

lm-app-towton-numbers.note: The Trust rejects inflated figures. The app already calls its army and casualty numbers chroniclers’ estimates; no exact army-size claim is verified. A source-linked numerical-claims table would be enrichment.

lm-app-welsh-acts.note: OpenLearn distinguishes 1536 and 1543. The current app already writes 1535–6 and 1542–3, preserving statutory/common dating conventions. The later court-system detail does not invalidate its 1536 display start.

lm-app-whitby-approx.note: The current summary says about 657 and about 1078. The separate ninth-century abandonment problem remains N21.

pr-cmp-arbor-low-certainty.note: EH confirms cumulative construction and later monuments. The app’s broad phase does not expressly say every feature existed unchanged for the entire millennium; its uncertainty already says not closely dated.

pr-cmp-barclodiad-fabric.note: Cadw identifies the present mound as reconstruction, but standing carved stones are real evidence. The app has a national point, not a detailed mound model. Downgrading all evidence to reconstructed solely on the present envelope would conflate fabric components.

pr-cmp-castlerigg-end.note: The current transition is from Stone circle to Standing monument, with low confidence and explicit dating uncertainty. Unlike Disused tomb, that label does not assert ceremonial cessation. No rejection is recorded.

pr-cmp-pentre-end.note: The phase explicitly says Disused tomb from 3000 BCE, without an end-of-use source.

pr-cmp-seahenge-end.note: Norfolk confirms timber felling in 2049 BCE. The current app explicitly says use duration is unknown and the endpoint nominal. No replacement ceremonial end is justified.

pr-cmp-silbury-duration.note: The phrase Mound under construction across the entire dating bracket is stronger than a brief campaign somewhere within it.

pr-cmp-silchester-start.note: EH gives an establishment bracket of c.20–10 BCE and the app summary preserves it. The national phase says oppidum, not ten years under construction. The imported construction-duration objection does not fit this data shape.

pr-cmp-thornborough-end.note: EH explicitly describes early Bronze Age burial use, which Out of use from 2000 BCE obscures.
